 scaling_values : Scaling values, also known as "ParamBonus," are displayed as a letter ranging from "E" (lowest) to "S" (highest). Each letter represents a percentage of additional attack damage in relation to a particular stat (Strength, Dexterity, Intelligence or Faith).

title: Parameter Bonus
snippet:
Parameter Bonus -  Dark Souls - mechanic - stat_rating 
 stat_rating : The stats that improve damage aren't directly used in the calculations; instead, they are first converted to a *rating,* which increases very quickly at low stat levels but slows down after reaching certain "soft caps." All attributes use the same conversion table to determine the bonus they receive from scaling, and Humanity uses its own.

Between each of the data points in the conversion tables, scaling increases linearly. Standard, raw, and crystal weapons, as well as weapons upgraded with twinkling titanite, demon titanite, or dragon scales, use the first table for determining the bonus damage from attributes. Weapons ascended down the Magic, Enchanted, Divine, and Occult paths use the second table for determining bonus damage from attributes.

title: Parameter Bonus
snippet:
Parameter Bonus -  Dark Souls - mechanic - lead 
 lead : The **Parameter Bonus** rating, also known as **Scaling**, is a gameplay mechanic in *Dark Souls*. It indicates the level of bonus damage one can do with a weapon, based on the associated stats. This rating can be S, A, B, C, D or E (in order from most to least bonus for the associated skill).

Strength and Dexterity will increase the physical damage while Intelligence and Faith will increase the Magic, Fire, and Lightning damage.

Chaos weapons will scale with Humanity. This will increase all types damage.

title: Parameter Bonus
snippet:

 humanity_scaling : Humanity scaling is a unique bonus attributed Chaos weapons, Chaos Blade, Quelaag's Furysword, and Abyss Greatsword. It affects both all forms of attack of chaos weapons by providing an additional 21% attack power to each stat (equivalent to ParamBonus "E"). At 5 Humanity, a Chaos +5 weapon starts to overtake its Fire +10 counterpart (Chaos has higher Fire damage while Fire has higher physical damage) At 10 Humanity, a Chaos +5 weapon effectively has the same physical damage and about 16% more Fire damage than its Fire +10 counterpart

Humanity scaling is a hidden stat, meaning it is not actually displayed in-game. Normally, chaos weapons will not have any magic or lightning attack power, but magic attack can be obtained on a bow ascended down the chaos path by firing Moonlight Arrows.

title: Parameter Bonus
snippet:
Parameter Bonus -  Dark Souls - mechanic - overview 
 overview : Each weapon has:
Four base attack values: physical, magic, lightning, and fire. These are the numbers shown as the weapon's stats.
For bow, crossbows, and greatbows, the attack power granted by the ammunition used is added to the weapon's base attack power (show as a +X value in the equipment screen next to the base damage) and is further affected by scaling.
Five scaling values: Strength, Dexterity, Intelligence, Faith, and Humanity.
**The only weapons with Humanity scaling are Chaos weapons, and their scaling is always 0.21.
Each character has:
Five ratings: Strength, Dexterity, Intelligence, Faith, and Humanity. These are not equal to the stats in question, but are derived from them (see below).
With these all in mind, the formulae are laid out below.

BonusDexterity* = *BasePhysical* × *DexterityScaling* × *DexterityRating*
BonusDexterity* = 95 × 39% × 65% ≈ **24**
PhysicalRating* = *BasePhysical* + *BonusStrength* + *BonusDexterity* + *BonusChaosPhysical*

BonusFaith* = *BaseMagic* × *FaithScaling* × *FaithRating*
BonusFaith* = 115 × 84% × 80% ≈ **78**
MagicRating* = *BaseMagic* + *BonusIntelligence* + *BonusFaith*
MagicRating* = 115 + 0 + 78 = **193**
TotalAttackRating* = *PhysicalRating* + *MagicRating* + *FireRating* + *LightningRating*
TotalAttackRating* = 120 + 193 + 0 + 0 = **313**

Parameter Bonus (Dark Souls II) -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - strength_vs_dexterity 
 strength_vs_dexterity : It has been observed that at equal rating, Strength scaling will give about twice as much benefit as Dexterity scaling; or, to see it another way, dexterity scaling is equivalent to a "2-tier" lower Strength scaling. For example, D scaling with 40 Strength will give as much benefit as a B scaling with 40 Dexterity.

Because of this, "quality" C/C weapons will gain more benefit from "40 STR / 20 DEX" than "20 STR / 40 DEX".

title: Parameter Bonus (Dark Souls II)
snippet:
Parameter Bonus (Dark Souls II) -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - soft_caps 
 soft_caps : In terms of "return on investment" (for strength and scaling), unlike in *Dark Souls*, players get the "best" return on investment in the 30~40 range. The gains go something like this:
0~30 : 100%
30~40 : 150%
40~50 : 50%
50~60 : 25%
Where "100%" represents an arbitrary scale of what the player would get per point for a given rating.

In terms of scaling, it means the best gains are for "putting all your eggs in the same basket", with either "40/20" for Strength/quality or "20/40" for Dexterity, but never "30/30".

title: Parameter Bonus (Dark Souls II)
snippet:
Parameter Bonus (Dark Souls II) -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - base_damage 
 base_damage : Unlike in *Dark Souls*, weapon scaling does not consider a weapon's base damage. The damage boost depends entirely on the stat and the parameter. This has some ramifications:
Low damage weapons will benefit the most from scaling. In particular, weapons such as the Club will more than double its damage output. A Mundane Handmaid's Ladle can deal upward to 130 extra attack rating, when the weapon's base damage is only 10. On the other hand, weapons that deal high damage will benefit less from scaling. For example, a Giant Warrior Club will gain about +100 attack rating, when it's base attack rating is roughly 500~600.
Weapons with low base damage but high scaling still benefit from reinforcement since scaling values also increase incrementally at each upgrade level.

title: Parameter Bonus (Dark Souls II)
snippet:
Parameter Bonus (Dark Souls II) -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - lead 
 lead : **Parameter Bonus** (also known as **Scaling**) is a gameplay mechanic in *Dark Souls II* similar to the ones from the first game.

It is a rating ranging from "E" to "S" of how well a weapon synergizes with a specific stat. These stats include Strength, Dexterity, Magic (mainly Intelligence), Lightning (mainly Faith), Fire (mainly a combination of Intelligence and Faith) and Dark (lowest stat between Intelligence and Faith).

All the details are not completely known; in particular, how scaling works when there are multiple stats at once (such as for "quality" weapons).

Although this requires a high investment in levels into multiple stats, the benefit is that it allows high Faith builds to cast Sorceries with power on par with their Miracles.  lead : The **Assassin** is one of the classes in *Dark Souls 3*.

It is a Dexterity-based class with decent Attunement for Weapon Arts and spells and some Intelligence for Sorceries.

An unusually long Thrusting Sword, the Estoc is also quite strong and has a rare sweeping heavy attack for hitting several or agile foes easier, at the cost of not having an increased critical modifier for Ripostes and Backstabs. Additionally, its Weapon Art, Shield Splitter, helps with its bad damage to the stamina of blocking targets by partially bypassing the defences of the block instead.

Its Targeting Shield, while not very suitable for blocking, is one of the game's three parrying shields and as such its Parry starts slightly earlier yet ends as late as the regular parry.

The Assassin Set has only moderate physical defences but has good magic and fire defences, and high overall resistances against anything that isn't Bleed.

 lead : The **Cleric** is one of the classes in *Dark Souls 3*.

It is a Faith-focused class, with decent Attunement, Strength, and Luck. This makes them well-suited to a Miracle-heavy build, and to using the many Lightning-attuned weapons as they are often also have good Strength-scaling.

While it does indeed have spells, in the form of Heal (which heals) and Force (which throws enemies away from you), it does not have any that causes damage, with the earliest ones not being found until Cathedral of the Deep or Farron Keep. This means the class will have to focus primarily on weapons initially, and will do well to keep them upgraded as offensive Miracles consume a lot of Focus Points.

title: Cleric (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Cleric (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - trivia 
 trivia : This is the only spellcasting-focused starting class in Dark Souls 3 that doesn't have a damage-boosting ring. Presumably this is because the Cleric doesn't have a damaging Miracle equipped from the start, and the Morne's Ring can instead be found in the Road of Sacrifices.
This class has remained remarkably similar throughout the series, always carrying a Mace and the Heal Miracle.

title: Cleric (Dark Souls III)
snippet: The Cleric's Sacred Chime is a fairly good casting tool and is actually the strongest casting tool for Miracles from 45 to 49 Faith. Its Spell Buff (the stat that affects how strong scaling spells are) doesn't actually increase until at least 19 Faith has been reached. Its Weapon Art is Gentle Prayer, a regenerative effect that always restores 360 hp over the course of a minute as long as the Chime is held in an active hand (so replacing it with another item stops it, as does two-handing the item in the other hand). This effect will actually outheal the Heal Miracle by up to 20% until the Chime's Spell Buff reaches 120, and even afterwards it is a strong if slow alternative due to only having about a third the cost in Focus Points.

title: Cleric (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
The Cleric Set is a light, caster-type armor set and as such has low physical defences and high elemental defences, while also having high Poison and Curse resistances.

The first trainer for more Miracles is found in the Undead Settlement for further development.

title: Cleric (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
The Mace is an unexpectedly strong weapon for what may at first seem like a spellcasting class, but in reality it is often a **Cleric's** main armament. This is because Strike damage is often the strongest physical damage type as armored and skeletal enemies are weak to it (most other physical damage types have fewer enemies weak to them), strong Strength-scaling for easy damage increases, a fairly good moveset, and has a good Weapon Art for trading hits with opponents. How the Weapon Art works is that Perseverance adds a flat 45% extra absorption and causes the attacks of light weapons to bounce off the user, while also granting great Hyper Armor to prevent being staggered.

The Blue Wooden Shield is not very good, having only decent physical and magic defence with serviceable Stability. While it does have Parry (albeit the inferior Medium Shield version), a strong Weapon Skill shield like the early Silver Eagle Kite Shield would probably serve as a better replacement.

title: Crossbows (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Crossbows (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - weapon - lead 
 lead : **Crossbows** are a type of weapon in *Dark Souls III*.

Crossbows are a ranged weapon that have rather low Strength and Dexterity requirements and offer no scaling, making them ideal for builds that do not invest heavily into physical stats. Unlike bows and greatbows, crossbows can be held and fired in one hand, but require the player to reload between shots as indicated by an arrow head in the top portion of the weapon icon. This makes them ideal ranged weapons for engaging foes within lock-on range.

title: Crossbows (Dark Souls III)
snippet: Crossbows can be equipped in either the main hand or off hand. When two-handed, all crossbows have a "zoom" feature, activated by pressing the off-hand weak attack button (or block), that allows the player to manually aim their shots from a first-person point of view. It should be noted that different types of Bolts have varying ranges that add to a specific crossbow's range. This affects the accuracy of the projectile resulting in some shots seeming inaccurate (this does not affect locked-on shots). Range can also be increased by equipping the Hawk Ring.

title: Deprived (Dark Souls II)
snippet:
Deprived (Dark Souls II) -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - lead 
 lead : The **Deprived** is one of the classes in *Dark Souls 2*.

Unlike the other classes, it doesn't start with any weapons or Lifegems and only has the unequipped Imported Set as armor. Make sure to retrieve the Dagger found in the first side path of Things Betwixt as an initial weapon, while the Morning Star in Majula can be wielded two-handed with 2 more Strength and 1 more Dexterity. A Cleric's Sacred Chime can be found near the Morning Star if wanting to use Miracles, a Shield can be gained by either buying one of Maughlin the Armorer in Majula or be found on the path to Heide's Tower of Flame, and a Sorcerer's Staff can be found behind a hidden wall in the Forest of Fallen Giants.

The low level means leveling up is slightly cheaper than for any other class, and the all-6 statline serves as a decent base for a build focused on the Mundane infusion since that scales of the lowest stat.

title: Deprived (Dark Souls II)
snippet:

 starting_equipment : The Deprived does not have anything equipped upon creation, not even Lifegems. However, as with all starting classes in Dark Souls 2, the Imported Set worn before the character creation can be found unequipped in the character's inventory.

title: Deprived (Dark Souls II)
snippet: Its average Adaptability and Attunment means it actually starts with a decent, 8 i-frame roll.

title: Deprived (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Deprived (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - lead 
 lead : The **Deprived** is one of the classes in *Dark Souls 3*.

It has a complete lack of focus in its stats, with all of them being 10 at the start. In combination with its low level of 1 this makes it a flexible, if non-optimal base for any build or respec the player wishes to do.

The Club is a simple yet strong weapon thanks to its quick attack speed and good strike damage. Its Weapon Art, Warcry, further increases damage by 10% for 30 seconds, and replaces the jump of its heavy attack with a flurry of blows, turning it into a stronger yet similarly niche attack. Its main disadvantage is its heavy focus on Strength-scaling as that might limit build potential a bit.

title: Deprived (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
The Plank Shield however is pretty much useless for blocking and should be replaced as soon was possible, most likely by either the Large Leather Shield or by the Silver Eagle Kite Shield (though the latter requires an additional point in Strength to wield).

Its lonely Loincloth is rather insufficient as armor, serving only to gain the flat armor bonus for having something equipped in an armor slot, and to gain a small amount of elemental defence and Poison resistance. To fill the remaining slots and gain more of an armor bonus, the Sword Master outside Firelink Shrine drops the Master's Attire and the Master's Gloves, or the Chain Set can be bought from the Shrine Handmaid for 2,300 souls total. Pieces of the Deserter Set can also be gained in High Wall of Lothric by killing Hollow Soldiers.

snippet:
Dexterity (Dark Souls II) -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - general_information 
 general_information : Raising one's Dexterity value primarily increases their Dexterity Attack Bonus, the value of which is multiplied by a hidden modifier of a weapon when attacking. Raising Dexterity also boosts the player's HP and Physical Defense stat, as well as one's Poison and Bleed Bonuses slightly.

For the few weapons that do scale, the softcaps for Dexterity are **20/40/50** for the purposes of increasing physical attack. Since a majority of weapons do not scale well, it is not worth it to get to the physical damage scaling softcaps or go beyond the minimum stats to wield in these cases.

title: Dexterity (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Dexterity (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - soft_caps 
 soft_caps : As of the 1.32 Regulations patch, Dexterity has two soft caps: 40 and 80.

For most normal builds, the damage return for weapon attack rating stops at 40 Dexterity. This applies to both quality builds and Dexterity-focused builds.

When utilizing the Sharp infusion, scaling on weapons changes at high levels. Attack rating returns between 40 and 60 Dexterity are relatively poor, with most weapons only seeing an increase in 1 point of damage per level of investment. But past 60 Dexterity, scaling increases again, seeing gains of 3 to 5 damage per level up until roughly 80 Dexterity, where it will gradually fall off.

title: Dexterity (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Dexterity (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - lead 
 lead : **Dexterity** is a stat in *Dark Souls III* that increases attack damage with Dexterity-based weapons.

Dexterity increases damage done by weapons with a scaling mechanic. A letter denoting a weapon's specific scaling properties is noted beneath the weapon's required Dexterity stat. The letters range in order of effectiveness from **E**, **D**, **C**, **B**, **A**, and **S**.

Weapons with an **E** rating for scaling will receive a poor benefit from investment in Dexterity while weapons with an **S** rating receive the greatest benefit.

As is with every other stat in the game, it also has indirect bonuses such as increasing the player character's flat damage absorption. Notable among these indirect bonuses is a reduction to fall-damage with every level invested into Dexterity.

title: Faith (Dark Souls)
snippet:
Faith (Dark Souls) -  Dark Souls - mechanic - description 
 description : Faith is an attribute used to meet requirements for melee weapons, Talismans, and spells; Faith softcaps are **30/50**. Similar to Intelligence, the amount of damage you deal and the amount of HP you heal from healing based Miracles will correlate with the Talisman you are using rather than your overall point investment into Faith. Faith is also a weapon modifier, increasing magical damage for unique weapons (see Weapon Scaling) any weapon upgraded down the Divine or Occult paths. Faith also serves to boost your magic defense. You will want to meet but not exceed the requirements to use spells, weapons, and Talismans.

Faith also increases the lightning damage of the Dragonslayer Spear and the physical damage of the (cursed) Greatsword of Artorias.

title: Moonlight Greatsword (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Moonlight Greatsword (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : A time-honored classic returning from the previous *Souls* games, the Moonlight Greatsword is a strong weapon in the hands of a dedicated Sorcery caster.

Unlike its previous iterations, *Dark Souls III*'s Moonlight Greatsword inflicts both physical and Magic damage, as well as being given scaling in Strength, albeit poorly. However, this does not change the fact that the physical scaling should be ignored, outside of meeting the minimum wielding requirements, in favor of leveling Intelligence, as the Moonlight Greatsword has been traditionally built (though as is the case with most melee weapons, it only scales effectively up to 40 in the offensive stats). The physical damage component is useful when performing criticals, as both damage types are magnified during the attack, allowing it to more easily punch through foes' flat Defenses.

 description : Small straight sword excelling in thrusting attacks.

The shortsword is a light and easily wielded straight sword, due to its minimal attribute requirements.

title: Giant Warrior Club
snippet:
Giant Warrior Club -  Dark Souls II - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : Fully upgraded, the Giant Warrior Club ties with the Malformed Skull for the weapon with the highest physical attack rating in *Dark Souls II*, reaching a maximum of 520 damage. Ultimately, the Warrior Club hits harder than the Malformed Skull, as the former has an A scaling in Strength, whereas the latter has no attribute scaling bonuses. The base damage of the Giant Warrior Club can be further increased through a Raw infusion, to reach a maximum of 598 damage, but severely lowering the Strength scaling bonus to D.

The weapon also has the highest Strength requirement in the base game to wield one-handed, at 60 Strength. However, the Smelter Hammer from the DLC is higher, at 70 Strength. It is also the second heaviest weapon by a margin of 5 units, being outweighed by the Smelter Hammer.

The Giant Warrior Club uses regular Titanite to upgrade.

title: Strength (Dark Souls)
snippet:
Strength (Dark Souls) -  Dark Souls - mechanic - notes 
 notes : Bows do not benefit from two-handing for the purposes of requirements or scaling.
Apart from extra damage due to bonus strength scaling, two-handing a weapon also changes its moveset to use two-handed moves, which tend to have higher damage modifiers at the cost of increased stamina cost and lowered attack speed, although some large weapons actually benefit from increased attack speed. This damage modifier is called Motion Value and increases damage for two handed attacks on all weapons regardless of scaling. Only Strength scaling weapons gaining increased damage via the boost to scaling and Motion Value simultaneously.
The weapon with the highest strength requirement, Smough's Hammer, requires 58 strength to be wielded in one hand.
The highest Strength scaling weapon in the game is Demon's Greataxe when on the Standard path and Crystal infused at 125% Strength scaling.

title: Smelter Hammer
snippet:
Smelter Hammer -  Dark Souls II - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : The Smelter Hammer is the heaviest weapon available in *Dark Souls II*, outweighing the Giant Warrior Club by 5.0 units. It also has the highest Strength requirement out of all weapons in *Dark Souls II*, requiring 70 Strength to wield in one-hand; however, it can be used in a Power Stance at 99 Strength.

However, despite its high requirements, the Smelter Hammer is capable of massive damage, due to both its high base damage and decent Strength scaling.

title: Parameter Bonus (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Parameter Bonus (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - lead

title: Great Club (Dark Souls II)
snippet:
Great Club (Dark Souls II) -  Dark Souls II - weapon - notes 
 notes : Upgrades with Titanite.
Great Club+10 has 420 base damage and "A" in Strength scaling, which makes it a very reliable weapon for Strength-oriented builds.
The Great Club is one of the best poise-consuming weapons in the game, especially in association with the Stone Ring. The three only weapons leading to higher poise damage are the Giant Warrior Club, the Gyrm Great Hammer and the Smelter Hammer, which Weight and Strength requirements are significantly higher.

title: Demon's Catalyst
snippet:
Demon's Catalyst -  Dark Souls - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : The Demon's Catalyst is the second-heaviest catalyst in the game to the Manus Catalyst, which weighs one unit more. It has one of the lowest potential magic adjusts of any catalyst, being the lowest until 41 Intelligence where it surpasses the Oolacile Ivory Catalyst and Oolacile Catalyst. It trades these things for being a powerful melee weapon, dealing Fire and Thrust damage with its strong attack. The high strength and dexterity scaling will have a powerful effect on dark sorceries, as the physical damage dealt by those sorceries are boosted by those stats. Overall the Demon's Catalyst should be considered as a weapon that is effective with dark sorceries, but is not as effective with regular sorceries.

title: Claymore (Dark Souls II)
snippet:
Claymore (Dark Souls II) -  Dark Souls II - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : The Claymore is a utilitarian greatsword with a versatile moveset, good reach, fast swing-speed, and solid damage per hit. It has relatively low strength and dexterity requirements, making it a viable option for infusions, while the C/C scaling makes it a powerful weapon for dedicated quality builds. These traits lets it fill a similar role to the Bastard Sword which performs similarly, but sacrifices the thrusting attack and some damage for lower weight and slightly lower requirements.

The main drawback of the Claymore is that many greatswords found later in the game outclass it in terms of damage. With that said, the Claymore remains a dependable weapon throughout the game, and its relatively low requirements makes it an attractive choice if one does not want to invest stats into using the more powerful elemental greatswords.

title: Great Scythe
snippet:
Great Scythe -  Dark Souls - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : The Great Scythe deals decent damage, and its low requirements and weight make it easily accessible to most players, primarily scaling off Dexterity unlike the usual "Quality Scaling" of most weapons in the Halberd class. The fast and wide running attack and strong attacks make the Great Scythe a great weapon for "dead-angling", though this unintended mechanic has been removed in the Remastered version of the game.

title: Scholar's Candlestick
snippet:
Scholar's Candlestick -  Dark Souls III - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : This weapon offers unimpressive physical damage and has a high Faith requirement to wield despite not scaling with that stat; as such, it is generally considered a very poor weapon regardless of circumstances.

However, its main characteristic is that while wielded it increases the damage dealt by any offensive Sorceries by 10%, regardless of whether they deal Magic or Dark damage, and regardless of whether or not the player meets the wielding requirements. As it stacks with other spell-boosting equipment such as Bellowing Dragoncrest Ring and Crown of Dusk, it is considered a staple off-hand tool for any dedicated Sorcerer build.

title: Chaos Blade (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Chaos Blade (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : The Chaos Blade provides excellent base damage, Dexterity scaling and reach, emphasizing the natural strengths of the katana class. It provides this with modest stat requirements and a standard katana moveset. At high levels of dexterity its physical damage is only outperformed by the Frayed Blade and the buffed Bloodlust.

title: Infusion (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Infusion (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - lead 
 lead : **Infusion** is a gameplay mechanic in *Dark Souls III*. It is a form of weapon reinforcement. Infusing a weapon can be performed by talking with Blacksmith Andre and change the attributes of a weapon. For example, infusing a Scimitar with the Blessed infusion increases the scaling on that weapon for Faith, while reducing scaling for every other parameter.

title: Dark Pyromancy Flame
snippet:
Dark Pyromancy Flame -  Dark Souls II - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : The Dark Pyromancy Flame possesses several attributes which the normal flame does not: it has superior scaling, durability and deals greater base Fire damage.

However, the most interesting aspect of this flame is the fact that it scales with the level of hollowing the player has. When used in human form, the Dark Pyromancy Flame receives a damage penalty which almost nullifies its attack rating, and through this, the damage dealt by pyromancies. Inversely, dying multiple times will result in a far stronger flame, significantly boosting damage output.

Hollowing directly affects the standard scaling this weapon possesses, it losing 10% for each hollowing level under the standard max of 10 despite the menu implying differently.

title: Ring of the Embedded
snippet:
Ring of the Embedded -  Dark Souls II - ring - effect 
 effect : Increases Vigor, Endurance and Vitality by an amount that is inversely proportional to how high each attribute currently is. This means that this ring gives a smaller bonus the more points you have invested in those attributes.
Increases damage taken by 8.5%

title: Man-serpent Greatsword
snippet:
Man-serpent Greatsword -  Dark Souls - weapon - trivia 
 trivia : The sword is a near-duplicate of the Meat Cleaver from *Demon's Souls,* and has similar stat requirements, though it swings far faster, and its magic damage and Dex and Faith scaling were removed.
In the German version, this sword is just called "Schlangenschwert", which literally translates to "Snakesword."

title: Possessed Armor Greatbow
snippet:
Possessed Armor Greatbow -  Dark Souls II - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : The Possessed Armor Greatbow has innate Dark damage and scaling, and is the only greatbow in the game that has split-damage types; the other greatbows will require an infusion for this effect.

Despite not using a stabilizing anchor, this greatbow has a similar rate of fire to that of the Dragonslayer Greatbow, although the drawing animation is similar to the Alonne Greatbow's. Essentially, this greatbow is the dexterity-oriented variant of the Dragonslayer Greatbow, as both have the same weight, durability, and maximum shot range; the only differences are the scaling and stat requirements.

While dark greatarrows do not exist in the game, the dark damage inflicted by this greatbow carries onto other greatarrows, allowing even the Iron and Destructive Greatarrows to damage an enemy attempting to block the shot, though the damage inflicted will be low.

title: Drakeblood Greatsword
snippet:
Drakeblood Greatsword -  Dark Souls II - weapon - trivia 
 trivia : The Drakeblood Greatsword can deal every damage type, except status effects, at once by infusing it with either Fire or Dark and using a weapon buff to apply the last element. However, the damage dealt will be minimal, which means it isn't viable for any actual use.
Despite dealing both Magic and Lightning damage, the Drakeblood Greatsword does not have an Intelligence or Faith requirement, nor does it have any scaling in said stats.

title: Onyx Blade
snippet:
Onyx Blade -  Dark Souls III - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : A weapon tailor-fit for Pyromancy builds, the Onyx Blade specializes in dealing strong elemental damage.

With stat requirements that diverge greatly from those of other greatswords, this weapon can only be properly wielded by builds with high investment in Intelligence and Faith, both of which fuel its Dark damage output. As its scaling in Strength and Dexterity is rather poor, those stats are best left as low as possible, as they do not benefit the weapon.

Borrowing its moveset from the Claymore, the Onyx Blade grants its wielder strong area coverage with its swings as well as thrusting attacks to give it formidable reach. In terms of length, it is the longest greatsword in the game, tied with the Wolf Knight's Greatsword. This gives it a tremendous advantage in that it can dictate the terms of a battle by preventing foes from easily approaching to attack.

title: Great Machete
snippet:
Great Machete -  Dark Souls II - weapon - description 
 description : The Great Machete is a Reaper-type weapon. Due to the fact that its Strength scaling is superior to its Dexterity scaling, it is one of the better Reapers for Strength builds, and has lower requirements than the Bone Scythe.

title: Karmic Justice
snippet:
Karmic Justice -  Dark Souls - spell - general_information 
 general_information : Karmic Justice acts as a sort of auto-defense miracle; it unleashes a powerful shockwave in all directions once it is triggered, dealing damage and knockback to hostiles. The damage dealt by the miracle is dependent on the magic adjust of the weapon in the player's right hand, as well as if they are wearing items like the Crown of Dusk and Red Tearstone Ring. The explosion has a base magic attack power of 300, and is affected by the intelligence and faith scaling of the weapon equipped in your right hand when the explosion occurs.

All weapons have a MagAdjust stat, but it is only visible on weapons that can cast spells. Any weapon that does not have any Intelligence or Faith scaling will have a MagAdjust of 100. Weapons that have Intelligence and/or Faith scaling, such as any Divine weapon, will affect the damage of Karmic Justice.

title: Dark (Dark Souls II)
snippet:
Dark (Dark Souls II) -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - infusion 
 infusion : Steady Hand McDuff can infuse most weapons with Dark through the use of a Darknight Stone. Once a weapon is infused, the Dark icon () will be displayed next to its image in the HUD.

Uninfused weapons imbued with Dark gain a fixed Dark Damage value (which scales with the Dark Attack Bonus), but the base physical damage is lowered by 30%, as is the base scaling. For example, if a regular weapon that deals 100 physical damage is infused with Dark, its stats switch over to 70 physical damage and 70 Dark Damage.
Weapons with innate Dark Damage gain an additional Dark scaling and a 44% damage increase to Dark, but the base physical damage is lowered by 5%, as is the current scaling.
Armor or shields gain additional Dark resistance while lowering other resistances.

title: Longsword
snippet:
Longsword -  Dark Souls - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : As the archetypical straight sword, the Longsword features slightly lower base damage, the same "Quality" scaling values as most other Straight Swords, a versatile moveset, and low stat requirements. Although it will perform admirably in any situation, its jack-of-all-trades nature means it will likely be outperformed by other Straight Swords that have higher base damage.

title: Straight Swords (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Straight Swords (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - weapon - lead 
 lead : **Straight Swords** are a type of weapon in *Dark Souls III*. They boast a variety of attacks from lunging slashes to thrusts, combined with fast attack speed, strong damage output and long reach, making them one of the strongest weapon classes in the game. Straight swords tend to have low Stat requirements, making them an excellent weapon of choice for generally any build when combined with the right infusion.

title: Painting Guardian Sword
snippet:
Painting Guardian Sword -  Dark Souls - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : The high DPS and swing speed of this sword is slightly offset by its short reach though it is only a tiny bit shorter than Falchion. The Painting Guardian Sword inflicts Bleed. It has the second highest Dexterity scaling of any melee weapon in the game behind Dark Silver Tracer, though PGS has superior damage potential. The Painting Guardian Sword is one of the fastest attacking weapon in the game, and is one of the best weapons for buffing with Spell Buffs or Resins.

title: Parameter Bonus (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Parameter Bonus (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - notes 
 notes : Weapons with non-scaling elemental damage will interact with both weapon buffs and infusions.
**For example, one can infuse a Drakeblood Greatsword with Chaos or Dark to add scaling to the pre-existing magic and lightning damage, as well as the added fire or dark damage.
**Similarly, one can cast Blessed Weapon on a Lothric Knight Greatsword to add Faith scaling to both the physical and lightning damage of the weapon.

title: Great Magic Weapon (Dark Souls II)
snippet:
Great Magic Weapon (Dark Souls II) -  Dark Souls II - spell - effect 
 effect : Applies a Magic buff to the weapon in the hand opposite the staff used to cast the spell. This is the intermediate sorcery weapon buff, between the Magic and Crystal variants, and as such has a moderate amount of casts, medium duration, and decent requirements. This places it in a somewhat awkward spot between the ease of acquisition and use of Magic Weapon and the power of Crystal Magic Weapon that makes it more suitable for a character with middling amounts of Intelligence, such as a character adding some decently powerful spells to their weapon usage.

The total bonus is difficult to calculate, but is roughly 20% of the sum (30 + weapon's Magic scaling * character's Magic bonus + weapon's Base damage), with a small additional damage bonus on Magic infused weapons.

title: Strength (Dark Souls)
snippet:
Strength (Dark Souls) -  Dark Souls - mechanic - description 
 description : Strength is an attribute used to meet requirements and increase damage to weapons that scale with Strength. Major softcaps are **27** when two-handing, and **40** overall. Some weapons like Great Club and Murakumo would benefit from having 28 strength instead of 27 since that is their one handed requirement.

Your Strength level is given a 1.5x multiplier when two-handing your right hand weapon for the purposes of weapon scaling and requirements. Anything higher than 27 is usually unnecessary outside of reaching the requirement to one hand your weapon. This is because at 27 strength, two handing will reach the optimal scaling soft cap of 40 (27 * 1.5 = 40.5, rounded down to 40). This is why 40/40 quality builds are generally not attainable or advisable in the first NG cycle, as the 13 points invested into strength is wasteful when you can just two hand.

title: Bandit's Knife
snippet:
Bandit's Knife -  Dark Souls - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : The Bandit's Knife deals low damage, but makes up for it in terms of critical rate. In terms of its Critical Modifier on backstab/riposte, the Bandit's Knife is second only to the Dark Silver Tracer. Do not mistake a high Critical Modifier for dealing the most damage on crits, as weapons with high base damage and scaling will perform better. The Bandit's Knife deals Bleed at a rate of 30 per strike, and can also be Enchanted with weapon buffs.

title: Shortsword (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Shortsword (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : The Shortsword is the second-lightest straight sword in the game, tied with the Cleric's Candlestick and beaten only by the Broken Straight Sword. Additionally, it ties with several other straight swords for having the lowest Strength wielding requirement. In exchange, it has rather short attack range and its damage output is mediocre for a weapon of its class. These combined characteristics make the Shortsword ideal for players who do not prioritize melee combat or have low investment in Vitality, but still want a reliable combat option in a pinch.

The Shortsword shares the same moveset as the Lothric Knight Sword, in particular its thrusting strong attacks. This makes the Leo Ring a handy complement.

title: Flamberge (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Flamberge (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : Despite having an average moveset, the Flamberge excels in its raw damage, while also being the only greatsword to inflict bleed and dealing purely Slash damage (with exception of the Stance strong attack, which deals Thrust damage).

This raw damage does have the penalty of a very poor scaling, but it is still very good, and its minimal requirements to wield it properly might make it an attractive choice for any player.

title: Light Crossbow (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Light Crossbow (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : The smallest crossbow available, the Light Crossbow is noteworthy in its ubiquity and ease of availability.

With its extremely low stat requirements and very light weight, every class in the game is capable of wielding this weapon at base Strength and Dexterity, with the majority of them being able to wield it in only one hand at those same stats. Because crossbows have no scaling, this makes the Light Crossbow useful in that it provides a form of ranged physical damage that does not require investment in physical damage stats. In particular, this is useful on builds that do not level Strength or Dexterity past nominal amounts, such as casters.

While it is not the most fearsome weapon, the Light Crossbow's ease of use makes it a worthy tool to consider carrying for whenever situations requiring the use of ranged attacks present themselves.

title: Ivory Straight Sword
snippet:
Ivory Straight Sword -  Dark Souls II - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : The Ivory Straight Sword is a very unusual weapon, as it is the only straight sword to deal Strike damage, and each attack consumes ten durability without the use of a Bracing Knuckle Ring. It also has the lowest stability of any weapon in the game, making it inefficient for blocking, and it is considered the second lightest weapon in the game, just behind the Handmaid's Ladle.

One of the other major drawbacks of the Ivory Straight Sword is without a doubt its requirements, as it is necessary to possess points in Dexterity, and the weapon possesses no scaling and cannot be buffed or infused, thus severely limiting its potential in combat. It can, however, be used in conjunction with Flynn's Ring and Ring of Blades, with their full effect, thus augmenting its damage a by a maximum of 100 damage.

title: Simple Gem
snippet:
Simple Gem -  Dark Souls III - item - usage 
 usage : Infuses weapons with Magic damage, granting Intelligence scaling but reducing Strength and Dexterity scaling, as well as reducing base damage. Compared to the Crystal infusion, the scaling is higher in all areas, but the base damage of the weapon is lower, meaning that the weapon will do less damage overall.

The benefit of the Simple infusion is that when wielded, the weapon slowly regenerates FP at a rate of about 1 FP per 5 seconds, or 0.2 FP per second. Reinforcing it will reduce the tick interval by roughly 0.217 seconds per upgrade level. At +10 reinforcement, a Simple weapon will replenish 1 FP per 2.85 seconds, or roughly 0.35 FP per second.
